source.title: Psychological anchoring effect and cross section of cryptocurrency returns

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies trading nearer to their trailing 52-week high subsequently outperform those far below the high because investor anchoring induces delayed incorporation of information.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each Monday retain the top 50 contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume among assets with exact daily history for the required high-window.
feature: NearnessL = prior completed UTC-day close divided by the maximum completed UTC-day close over the prior L days.
signal_direction: Long highest NearnessL quintile; short lowest NearnessL quintile.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long/short, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: Compute at Monday 00:00 UTC using data through Sunday. Enter Monday open and exit next Monday open; a preregistered robustness test delays entry to Tuesday open and exits the following Tuesday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive high-minus-low weekly spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 lookbacks positive after base costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive total return at 2x costs; at least 2/3 lookbacks positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; exclude BTC/ETH positive; exclude strongest contributor positive; one-day delayed implementation positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The paper reports a value-weighted cANCHOR spread of roughly 130 bps per week. Market capitalization is unavailable in the futures OHLCV panel, so this preregistration uses equal weights within point-in-time liquidity-screened quintiles.
